The Fox and the Mask

A F
OX
 had by some means got into the store-room of a theatre. Suddenly he observed a face glaring down on him and began to be very frightened; but looking more closely he found it was only a Mask such as actors use to put over their face. “Ah,” said the Fox, “you look very fine; it is a pity you have not got any brains.”
“OUTSIDE SHOW IS A POOR SUBSTITUTE FOR INNER WORTH.”
